answer: Persistent Work Relic Ledger. Each identity must accumulate a signed history of completed tasks, anchored to a summit checkpoint that only advances when prior work verifies. Cloning a wallet starts it at zero history, so it cannot access higher-tier contracts. A mesa of validators audits task traces; fraudulent clones get their operator's shared resource pool frozen across all linked wallets. The relic of past work is non-transferable, forcing attackers to redo real labor per clone, costing time and compute proportional to tier depth.
